title: LAN Chile 107
summary: LAN-Chile Flight 107, a Douglas DC-6B-404 on a scheduled international flight from Santiago to Buenos Aires, crashed into La Corona Mountain in the Las Melosas area of the Andes at flight level 120 on 6 February 1965, about 1,200 feet below the summit. All 88 occupants were killed, including 22 players and staff of Santiago's Antonio Varas football team traveling to a match in Montevideo. The accident investigation board attributed the crash to the pilot in command choosing a route that followed neither the approved flight plan nor the airline's operations manual, and it ruled that weather was not a factor.
probable_cause: The accident investigation board attributed the accident to the pilot in command, who chose to follow a route that was neither in accordance with the approved flight plan nor the airline's operations manual; weather was not a factor in the crash.

factors.evidence: chose to follow a route that was neither in accordance with the approved flight plan
it crashed into the side of La Corona Mountain, approximately 1200 ft below its summit

events.text: The DC-6 departed Santiago-Los Cerrillos Airport on the morning of 6 February with 80 passengers and seven crew members bound for Ezeiza, near Buenos Aires.
The pilot in command chose to follow a route that was neither in accordance with the approved flight plan nor the airline's operations manual.
When the aircraft was at flight level 120 in the Las Melosas area of the Andes, it crashed into the side of La Corona Mountain, approximately 1200 ft below its summit; there were no survivors.

notes: Investigating agency not named in the text.

title: Eastern Air Lines 663
summary: Eastern Air Lines Flight 663, a DC-7 departing Boston for Atlanta, was executing a Dutch seven departure over the Atlantic when air traffic control detected a potential conflict with Pan Am Flight 212 at a lower altitude. Flight 663 initiated an extreme right turn to avoid collision, but could not recover from the steep bank and plunged into the Atlantic Ocean. All 84 occupants were killed. The CAB determined that evasive maneuvers in dark night conditions with no visible horizon caused spatial disorientation.
probable_cause: evasive maneuvers undertaken by Flight 663 to avoid an oncoming Pan Am Boeing 707 in dark night conditions with no visible horizon caused the pilot to suffer spatial disorientation and loss of control

factors.evidence: The night of February 8 was dark, with no visible moon or stars and no visible horizon
The CAB determined that the evasive maneuvers taken by the pilot of Flight 663 caused spatial disorientation

events.text: Flight 663 departed JFK at 6:20 pm EST on an instrument flight rules clearance to Byrd Field
ATC radioed Flight 663 that Pan Am Flight 212 was in the airspace at 2 o'clock position
The night was dark with no visible moon or stars and no visible horizon as evasive maneuvers commenced
Eastern 663 began an extreme right turn to pass safely from the oncoming aircraft

title: Pakistan International Airlines 705
summary: PK705 crashed on final approach to Cairo International Airport on 20 May 1965, killing 121 of the 127 aboard. The pilot reported problems with the flaps shortly before the Boeing 720 crashed southeast of the airport and exploded into flames. Investigators found the aircraft did not maintain adequate height for the circuit and continued descending until it contacted the ground; the reason for that abnormal descent could not be determined.
probable_cause: The aircraft did not maintain the adequate height for the circuit and continued to descend until it contacted the ground; the reason for that abnormal continuation of descent is unknown.

factors.evidence: the pilot reported problems with the flaps
the aircraft did not maintain the adequate height for the circuit and continued to descend until it contacted the ground
the aircraft crashed southeast of the airport and broke up as it exploded into flames

events.text: On final approach to Cairo International Airport, the pilot reported problems with the flaps.
The aircraft did not maintain the adequate height for the circuit and continued to descend toward the ground.
The aircraft crashed southeast of the airport and broke up as it exploded into flames; six passengers were thrown clear of the wreckage but everyone else aboard was killed.

notes: Investigation could not determine the reason for the abnormal continuation of descent.
No investigating agency named in the text.
